Start here: Testing programs

Source: vignettes/articles/for-practitioners.Rmd
for-practitioners.Rmd

Operational work needs decisions you can defend and reports that non-statisticians can read. mirtverse wraps mirt’s estimation in a documented workflow: Each step checks the results and raises flags that a person reviews before the next step.

Your path in three steps

Read the case study first. It follows a fictional certification board through eight decisions and ends with a technical report you can download.

1. Walk through the assessment pipeline. mv_pipeline() takes a test through 13 stages, from the blueprint to bank monitoring. The pipeline article runs a full example:

library(mirtverse)
# certexam is a built-in certification exam with a scoring key
p <- mv_pipeline("Certification exam, form A")
p <- add_responses(p, certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key)
p <- calibrate(p)          # fits the model and flags miskeys, misfit and DIF
flags(p)                   # what needs a decision before you move on

2. Check fairness and precision. DIF in one call, item health cards for review meetings, and information and conditional precision at the cut score:

mod <- p$model             # an ordinary mirt model
item_card(mod, "Q14")      # one-page review of a flagged item
res <- dif(scored, group = gender)   # your scored 0/1 data and a grouping variable
gg_dif(res)

3. Report to people who do not use R. A technical report from the pipeline, a static HTML report, or an interactive dashboard that runs in any browser:

pipeline_report(p, file = "technical-report.html")
export_dashboard(mod, "results.html", format = "html")

Open the live example dashboard to see what your stakeholders would get.

Why you can trust the numbers

  • mirtverse never changes how models are estimated; every result comes from mirt, and every function accepts an ordinary mirt() model.
  • The package has an automated test suite and passes R CMD check on every change (check status).
  • Every flag rule is listed by mv_rules() and can be changed, and every decision you acknowledge is recorded in the report.
  • The workbench and mv_ask() show the R code they run, so analyses can be reviewed and rerun.
